chunks: As for the right of your property,

is that you take it only from what is lawful, and spend it only in what is proper, and do not prefer above yourself those who will not praise you. Act with it in obedience to your Lord and do not be miserly with it, lest you fall back into regret and remorse while suffering the ill consequence. And there is no strength save in God.
ai.seo_question: What are the ethical obligations regarding the acquisition and spending of wealth in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin expands the concept of wealth rights by emphasizing not just lawful acquisition but the spiritual integrity of expenditure, urging believers to avoid ostentation and preferential treatment based on flattery. This guidance transforms material possession into an act of worship, warning that miserliness incurs both spiritual regret and divine accountability, a theme deeply rooted in Shia ethical jurisprudence. The passage serves as a practical framework for balancing worldly stewardship with otherworldly devotion.
